review: Meson fs is already imported at meson.build:20. fs.name is the native basename operation; group naming now agrees with qapi generated trace header consumers on Windows. On POSIX it preserves the previous final slash-component behavior for these generated files. The prior basename collision behavior is unchanged; source trace subdirectory groups are untouched.

tracetool.py passes ordinary argv strings to read_events and out_open. out_open still opens the original filename; only the emitted out_filename metadata is normalized. Every out_filename consumer is a generated #line directive in log/ftrace/syslog.

Each backend normalizes the existing relpath result only for C #line metadata. Windows native backslashes become forward slashes, preventing unknown C escapes while preserving drive and relative components; existing forward slashes remain. On POSIX os.sep is already slash so paths and literal backslash filename characters are unchanged.

Backend import os.path already binds the os module, therefore os.sep is available without an additional backend import. The added import os in tracetool/__init__.py supplies the new direct reference there.

All four changed Python modules are AST-parsed from bytes, without imports/calls. Exact before/after snapshots contain only the requested native-basename or metadata separator changes. No file I/O target, trace event name/payload, guest behavior, peripheral logic or firmware is changed by these five edits.

Recorded failed build01 matches missing expected trace-qapi_commands_authz_trace_events.h; recorded failed build02 reaches that correctly named generated header and reports unknown escape sequence \q in #line. This review does not infer build03 success or any emulator/production qualification.
scope_limits: Source review only: no Meson/tracetool execution, compilation, tests, QEMU, Git or external edits.

This addresses native path separators in the existing ordinary build paths; general C string escaping for quotes/control characters and relpath across different Windows drives were preexisting unsupported edge cases and are not claimed fixed.
Actual Windows rebuild and regression results remain root-owned; no POSIX runtime build is claimed.

primary_documentation.supports: Official fs.name documentation defines basename/last-component semantics; fs module exists since0.53.0. QEMU already imports this module.
